samples.summary: Design doc still describes the undo floor as identity-only; the delta added a depth fallback, an identity-verification probe and a cap latch
samples.evidence: docs-collaboration.md:400-412 ("The undo floor is an entry, not a depth") states `YorkieDocStore` "holds the floor by the identity of the stack's top entry ... An entry that has itself been dropped is simply not found, which is exactly the 'the floor is gone, so everything left is above it' answer a depth cannot give." After this delta that is only half the behaviour: `undoFloorDepth`/`undoFloorIdentityUsable` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:617, 625) make the depth comparison the fallback, and a not-found entry now only means "floor gone" when `stack.length >= YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3062-3071). Nested/top-level doc-ref CI does not catch prose drift.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. editor.ts:3313-3318 defines `getDoc: () => doc` and `getStore: () => (readOnly ? readStore : pageSetupGuardedStore)` with no `disposed` check, while dispose() (editor.ts:4434-4444) only calls neuterMutations(api), which rewrites the MUTATING_METHODS names on `api` itself (editor.ts:1042-1072) and leaves `doc`/`docStore` writable. The `readOnlyDocStore` coverage cited in the comment at editor.ts:4503-4509 is construction-time only (editor.ts:1123), so it does nothing for a writable editor that is later disposed — which the dispose comment at 4435-4442 says is precisely the revocation moment. A real holder writes around it: docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68 captures `editor.getDoc()` in a ref and FindReplaceState.replaceActive/replaceAll/replaceMatch (find-replace.ts:57-87) call doc.deleteText/insertText directly, never through EditorAPI; and such a write still lands in the CRDT because YorkieDocStore.dispose() (yorkie-doc-store.ts:689-693) only unsubscribes and leaves mutators live. The find bar's own `readOnly` prop gate (docs-find-bar.tsx:134,143) covers the permission-downgrade path but is a different flag from disposal and does not cover dispose triggered by the `doc`/unmount deps (docs-view.tsx:565, deps at :590), so I cannot show the bypass is unreachable. Only the secondary evidence (hunt/bridge.ts:386, a read-only `canUndo()`) is weak; the primary site stands. Guard-with-a-bypass is squarely in the blast-radius lane at major.

finding.summary: Undo floor now depends on `getUndoStackForTest()` returning identity-stable entries
finding.evidence: `canUndo()` was changed to `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2997-3004), which only works if the SDK's `getUndoStackForTest()` hands back the live stack (or at least the same inner entry objects) on every call. It is a `...ForTest` accessor, i.e. explicitly not a stable public contract, and the SDK is not vendored in this tree so I could not confirm it. If it ever returns copied entries, `lastIndexOf` is always `-1`, `canUndo()` answers `true` for the initial-load prefix, and a user can undo past `setDocument()` — the exact destruction the floor exists to prevent (the write it undoes is `writeFullDocument`, and the cursor still references blocks it removes). The old `length > undoFloor` comparison could not fail that way. Worth pinning with a test that asserts a floor-only stack reports `canUndo() === false` through this new code path (the added test only covers the overflow direction).

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that canUndo() unconditionally trusts getUndoStackForTest() identity, so a copying accessor yields lastIndexOf === -1 and canUndo() === true past the floor — does not hold in this tree. (a) The quoted expression `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1` at 2997-3004 is not present; the real code is at 3043-3076 and reads `const index = stack.lastIndexOf(...); if (index >= 0) return stack.length > index + 1;` (3051-3056). (b) Identity is verified rather than assumed: markUndoFloor() re-reads the accessor and compares entry identity, setting `undoFloorIdentityUsable` (931-933). (c) The identity branch is gated on that flag at 3047, so with a copying accessor it is never entered. (d) The fallback at 3075 is exactly the old `stack.length > undoFloorDepth` comparison, with undoFloorDepth = stack.length set at mark time (925), so a floor-only stack returns false — degrading to refusing an undo, never to permitting one past setDocument(). The only undo entry point in this store (3029-3034) is gated by canUndo(); other history.undo() sites are unrelated stores. The remaining suggestion (add a floor-only regression test) is test-adequacy, not blast-radius.
